title: Le présent de l'indicatif
ruleNote: The present tense — what is happening now or habitually. Regular verbs follow -ER/-IR/-RE patterns; the most common verbs (être, avoir, aller, faire) are irregular.

exercises.translation: I am a student in Paris.
exercises.hint: 'je' form of the irregular verb être.
exercises.explanation: With 'je', être is irregular: je suis.

exercises.translation: You are very kind.
exercises.hint: 'tu' form of the irregular verb être.
exercises.explanation: With 'tu', être is irregular: tu es.

exercises.translation: He is in the kitchen.
exercises.hint: 'il' form of the irregular verb être.
exercises.explanation: With 'il', être is irregular: il est.

exercises.translation: We are late.
exercises.hint: 'nous' form of the irregular verb être.
exercises.explanation: With 'nous', être is irregular: nous sommes.

exercises.translation: You are very patient.
exercises.hint: 'vous' form of the irregular verb être.
exercises.explanation: With 'vous', être is irregular: vous êtes.

exercises.translation: They are at home.
exercises.hint: 'ils' form of the irregular verb être.
exercises.explanation: With 'ils', être is irregular: ils sont.

exercises.translation: I have a black dog.
exercises.hint: 'je' form of the irregular verb avoir.
exercises.explanation: With 'je', avoir is irregular: j'ai.

exercises.translation: You are right.
exercises.hint: 'tu' form of the irregular verb avoir.
exercises.explanation: With 'tu', avoir is irregular: tu as.

exercises.translation: He has two brothers.
exercises.hint: 'il' form of the irregular verb avoir.
exercises.explanation: With 'il', avoir is irregular: il a.

exercises.translation: We have a big garden.
exercises.hint: 'nous' form of the irregular verb avoir.
exercises.explanation: With 'nous', avoir is irregular: nous avons.

exercises.translation: You have a nice car.
exercises.hint: 'vous' form of the irregular verb avoir.
exercises.explanation: With 'vous', avoir is irregular: vous avez.

exercises.translation: They have a lot of friends.
exercises.hint: 'ils' form of the irregular verb avoir.
exercises.explanation: With 'ils', avoir is irregular: ils ont.

exercises.translation: I talk with my friends.
exercises.hint: je form of an -ER verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'je', a regular -ER verb takes the -e ending: parle.

exercises.translation: You speak French very well.
exercises.hint: tu form of an -ER verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'tu', a regular -ER verb takes the -es ending: parles.

exercises.translation: He is talking on the phone.
exercises.hint: il form of an -ER verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'il', a regular -ER verb takes the -e ending: parle.

exercises.translation: We talk about our vacation.
exercises.hint: nous form of an -ER verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'nous', a regular -ER verb takes the -ons ending: parlons.

exercises.translation: You speak too fast for me.
exercises.hint: vous form of an -ER verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'vous', a regular -ER verb takes the -ez ending: parlez.

exercises.translation: They speak Spanish at home.
exercises.hint: ils form of an -ER verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'ils', a regular -ER verb takes the -ent ending: parlent.

exercises.translation: I finish my work at noon.
exercises.hint: je form of an -IR verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'je', a regular -IR verb takes the -is ending: finis.

exercises.translation: You always finish your homework.
exercises.hint: tu form of an -IR verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'tu', a regular -IR verb takes the -is ending: finis.

exercises.translation: He finishes the book tonight.
exercises.hint: il form of an -IR verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'il', a regular -IR verb takes the -it ending: finit.

exercises.translation: We finish the meal together.
exercises.hint: nous form of an -IR verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'nous', a regular -IR verb takes the -issons ending: finissons.

exercises.prompt: Vous ___ la réunion à cinq heures. (finir)
exercises.translation: You finish the meeting at five o'clock.
exercises.hint: vous form of an -IR verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'vous', a regular -IR verb takes the -issez ending: finissez.

exercises.translation: They finish their studies this year.
exercises.hint: ils form of an -IR verb in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'ils', a regular -IR verb takes the -issent ending: finissent.

exercises.translation: I am going to school this morning.
exercises.hint: 'aller' is irregular; think of the 'je' form in the present.
exercises.explanation: With 'je', 'aller' in the present is 'vais' — an irregular stem, not 'all-'.

exercises.prompt: Tu ___ au marché avec ta mère. (aller)
exercises.translation: You are going to the market with your mother.
exercises.hint: 'aller' is irregular; the 'tu' form in the present ends in -s.
exercises.explanation: With 'tu', 'aller' in the present is 'vas' — irregular stem 'v-' plus -s.

exercises.translation: He goes to work by bus.
exercises.hint: 'aller' is irregular; the 'il' form in the present has no ending.
exercises.explanation: With 'il', 'aller' in the present is 'va' — irregular stem 'v-' with no added ending.

exercises.translation: We are going to the cinema tonight.
exercises.hint: 'aller' is irregular; the 'nous' form keeps the 'all-' stem and ends in -ons.
exercises.explanation: With 'nous', 'aller' in the present is 'allons' — the 'all-' stem plus -ons.

exercises.prompt: Vous ___ souvent à la plage en été. (aller)
exercises.translation: You often go to the beach in summer.
exercises.hint: 'aller' is irregular; the 'vous' form keeps the 'all-' stem and ends in -ez.
exercises.explanation: With 'vous', 'aller' in the present is 'allez' — the 'all-' stem plus -ez.

exercises.translation: They are going to the party on Saturday.
exercises.hint: 'aller' is irregular; the 'ils' form in the present ends in -ont.
exercises.explanation: With 'ils', 'aller' in the present is 'vont' — an irregular form ending in -ont.

exercises.prompt: Je ___ mes devoirs avant le dîner. (faire)
exercises.translation: I do my homework before dinner.
exercises.hint: 'faire' is irregular; the 'je' form in the present ends in -s.
exercises.explanation: With 'je', 'faire' in the present is 'fais' — irregular stem 'fai-' plus -s.

exercises.translation: You do sports on the weekend.
exercises.hint: 'faire' is irregular; the 'tu' form in the present ends in -s.
exercises.explanation: With 'tu', 'faire' in the present is 'fais' — irregular stem 'fai-' plus -s.

exercises.prompt: Il ___ un gâteau pour la fête. (faire)
exercises.translation: He is making a cake for the party.
exercises.hint: 'faire' is irregular; the 'il' form in the present ends in -t.
exercises.explanation: With 'il', 'faire' in the present is 'fait' — irregular stem 'fai-' plus -t.

exercises.prompt: Nous ___ la cuisine ensemble ce soir. (faire)
exercises.translation: We are cooking together tonight.
exercises.hint: 'faire' is irregular; the 'nous' form ends in -ons.
exercises.explanation: With 'nous', 'faire' in the present is 'faisons' — the 'fais-' stem plus -ons.

exercises.translation: You always make a lot of noise.
exercises.hint: 'faire' is irregular; the 'vous' form is an exception, not -ez.
exercises.explanation: With 'vous', 'faire' in the present is 'faites' — an irregular form ending in -tes.

exercises.prompt: Ils ___ leurs valises pour le voyage. (faire)
exercises.translation: They are packing their bags for the trip.
exercises.hint: 'faire' is irregular; the 'ils' form in the present ends in -ont.
exercises.explanation: With 'ils', 'faire' in the present is 'font' — an irregular form ending in -ont.
